solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, mirror symmetry); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In uncomplicated final part of course

parts.note: at home is a common sense of 'in', as in 'is she in?'
straight means simple or uncomplicated, as in a straight answer

explanation.surface: Something tucked inside the closing stretch of a simple course, like a lesson plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but supplies HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: On a racetrack the home straight is the last stretch before the finishing post.

clue.text: Payment arrangement cheaper? I rush, madly

indicators.note: done madly, the letters of the words before it are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopper hurries to sign up for an instalment deal, hoping it works out cheaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire purchase is the British name for buying goods by instalments, paying over time while using them.

clue.text: Wanting to see girl in capital of Germany

parts.note: miss is a title for, and so a word for, a young woman or girl

indicators.note: the capital, or head letter, of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone longing to visit a girl living in Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Germany' wants to be Berlin; it is only the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Something missing is lacking, which is the old sense of wanting, as in 'found wanting'.

clue.text: Problem involving credit leading to melée

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the problem's letters wrap round the credit

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set in school
CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: A dispute over credit escalates into a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum is a disorderly crowd pushing together, borrowed from rugby, so it fits a confused fight or melée.

clue.text: Sport and business degree? Here may be steps you can take

definitions.text: Here may be steps you can take

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the usual crossword sport
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: Career advice: combine sport with a business degree and see what steps open up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps you can take' reads like career moves; they are dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, so it is a place where dance steps are made.

clue.text: I modified using one? Very clever

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters of the two words after the I are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone proudly reports adapting one gadget and asks whether that counts as brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious describes inventive, original thinking, which is a strong form of cleverness.

clue.text: Government Minister? Sadly they care more about status, primarily

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled into another order
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of status is used

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that politicians care more about status than service.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes THEY CARE MORE plus S, the first letter of 'status'. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Secretary is a senior UK Cabinet minister responsible for policing, immigration and security.

clue.text: Unhappy year when kept outside confines of the stable

indicators.note: being kept outside means the first letters stand round the second piece

parts.note: unhappy means sad

indicators.note: the confines of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A miserable year for a horse shut out of its stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the stable' reads as a horse's home; 'the' gives its outer letters TE and 'stable' is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady and stable are synonyms meaning firm and not wobbling or changing.

clue.text: Sort to dance beside curious platform

indicators.note: making the letters dance shakes them out of their order into a new one

parts.note: rum is a British informal word for odd or curious

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a dance beside an odd stage.
explanation.walkthrough: SORT rearranged gives ROST; 'rum' meaning strange is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand for a speaker or conductor, a small platform.

clue.text: First pair of marines aboard harbour vessel, back in range

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read from right to left
being aboard means being inside the vessel, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tug is a small boat that tows ships in harbour

indicators.note: the first pair means the opening two letters of the word

explanation.surface: Two marines climb onto a tug and head back within range.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion comes first: 'aboard' puts the pair inside the boat, then 'back' turns the whole of TUMAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamut is the complete range or scope of something, as in 'the whole gamut of emotions'.

clue.text: Rigidly precise, restricting small source of coloured light

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the first word's letters close round the second

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and correct
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A fussy, exacting person keeps a small coloured lamp under control.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass prism splits white light into a spectrum, so it produces coloured light.

clue.text: It helps to forget different men in a large part of the world

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters are placed inside the continent

parts.words: a large part of the world
parts.note: Asia is the largest continent

indicators.note: made different, the letters of men are rearranged

explanation.surface: Travelling among different men across a vast continent helps someone forget the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' shuffles the men into MNE; 'It helps to forget' describes the answer playfully rather than naming a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, so it is literally the condition of forgetting.

clue.text: British avoiding showing intelligence? Correct

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: bright means clever, showing intelligence

explanation.surface: A jibe that Brits avoid looking clever, followed by agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and correct are synonyms meaning accurate or true.

clue.text: Faced with dilemma over fuss? That's a blow

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it comes first, above it

parts.note: being torn means unable to choose between two options
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: Someone torn over a fuss shrugs it off as a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's a blow' sounds like an expression of disappointment; it is a literal blow of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, so it literally blows.

clue.text: Bishop with crowd standing beside church yard in an irregular form

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a lot is a group or crowd of people

explanation.surface: A bishop and a crowd stand by the churchyard, oddly arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church yard' reads as one place; it splits into CH and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotchy skin or paint is patchy and uneven, marked in an irregular way.

clue.text: Horde of people, upset about defeat, to become more mature

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed letters surround the other piece
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a mob is a disorderly crowd
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: A crowd, upset at losing, needs to grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' flips the horde to read BOM, and the defeat sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to flower, and figuratively to develop and mature into one's potential.

clue.text: Comic greeting America, including North and South American cities

indicators.note: including means the first pieces close round the cities

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
US is the United States
LA (Los Angeles) is in North America, Rio (de Janeiro) in South America

explanation.surface: A comedian saying hello to America, name-checking cities on both continents.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarious means extremely funny, so it can stand for comic as an adjective.

clue.text: Free to fail, getting nothing twice

indicators.note: getting means taking in, so the extra letter goes inside the word

parts.note: to lose is to fail to win
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: Someone free to fail, ending up with nothing on two counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' says the extra O sits beside LOSE's own O, giving two together.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means not tied or held, so free, as in an animal on the loose.

clue.text: The writer recalled hugging large tree

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round, so the reversed letters enclose the other
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: An author remembers embracing a big tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a familiar deciduous tree, once common in English hedgerows.

clue.text: Doctor has to run a car?

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Asking whether a doctor really needs to run a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is a British informal word for a car, as in 'nice motor'.

clue.text: Snapshot, as it's developed, reveals store worker

indicators.note: a photo is developed, and here the letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A photo, once developed, shows who works in the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop assistant serves customers in a store, so is a retail worker.

clue.text: American uncle turning up in Damascus

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, so backwards
in shows the letters lie inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A relative from the States appearing in the Syrian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the personification of the US government, so the American uncle's name.

clue.text: Change with regard to group of students

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
a form is a school class, in British usage

explanation.surface: Changes made regarding a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to change something, usually to improve it.

clue.text: Month with other ranks for council official

parts.note: May is a month
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A month with the troops for a local councillor.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the elected head of a town or city council.
